subject: Your ChatGPT directory tracking + GitHub side data
text:
Hi,

I saw your weekly reports on the ChatGPT plugin directory. The +1,574 week was wild. I run PickAPlugin, which covers the other side: the open-source Codex and ChatGPT plugins that live on GitHub and never make it into the official directory.

We published a small data report on 339 of them (stars, licenses, install commands, plugin.json checks): https://pickaplugin.com/research/state-of-codex-plugins-2026

It's CC BY, so feel free to cite it in a guide or report if it's useful. And if a link swap between our sites makes sense to you, I'm up for it.

Aaron, PickAPlugin
https://pickaplugin.com

subject: Data for your Codex plugin marketplace guide
text:
Hi,

I came across your Codex plugin marketplace explainer. It's a clear write-up of how the install flow works.

I run PickAPlugin, a hand-sorted catalog of Codex and ChatGPT plugins. We pulled GitHub data on 339 plugin repos and published what we found, like 31% having no copyable install command and only 3 of 274 plugin.json files having hard errors: https://pickaplugin.com/research/state-of-codex-plugins-2026

If any of it fits your guides, it's CC BY, free to cite with a link.

Aaron, PickAPlugin
https://pickaplugin.com

subject: A possible item for AI Coding Weekly
text:
Hi,

I came across AI Coding Weekly and thought this might be useful for an issue. We looked at 339 open-source Codex and ChatGPT plugin repos: median 6 stars, 43% need an API key, and 16% haven't been touched in 90+ days.

Full write-up and charts: https://pickaplugin.com/research/state-of-codex-plugins-2026

It's CC BY, so use whatever helps. No worries if it's not a fit.

Aaron, PickAPlugin
https://pickaplugin.com

subject: Codex plugin numbers for the newsletter
text:
Hi,

PulseMCP has been a go-to MCP directory for a while. I run PickAPlugin, a hand-sorted catalog of ChatGPT and Codex plugins, and a lot of those plugins are really MCP servers in a wrapper.

We pulled data on 339 of them. 18% wire up a remote MCP server over HTTP, and 43% ask for an API key: https://pickaplugin.com/research/state-of-codex-plugins-2026

Might be a useful data point for a newsletter or post. It's CC BY, free to cite with a link.

Aaron, PickAPlugin
https://pickaplugin.com
